article_title: Preservice mathematics teachers’ noticing in AI-based simulations: transitions among attending, interpreting, and shaping
citation: Selen Galiç, Mathias Tejera, Sebastián Parodi, Markus Hohenwarter, Zsolt Lavicza. (2026). Preservice mathematics teachers' noticing in AI-based simulations: transitions among attending, interpreting, and shaping. ZDM – Mathematics Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11858-026-01805-4
title: Teacher Noticing of Rationality Framework (TNRF)
description: The TNRF builds on van Es and Sherin's expanded noticing framework of attending, interpreting, and shaping, and "extends van Es and Sherin's (2021) framework by specifying the object of noticing more precisely as students' mathematical thinking". It operationalises students' thinking through Habermas's theory of rationality as observable behaviours: justifying statements, selecting and using appropriate tools, and communicating with appropriate terminology and representations. Attending targets manifestations of rational behaviour rather than surface correctness; interpreting evaluates the quality of participation in mathematical practices; shaping structures conditions under which rational behaviour becomes visible.
requirements: Requires teachers' professional knowledge and an inquiry stance to interpret behaviours through the rationality lens rather than simple correctness judgments
constraints: The article applies the framework specifically to the equal-sign context, with coding adapted to the construct map of the equal sign (Matthews et al., 2012)
target_learning_goals: Noticing students' mathematical thinking in the context of the equal sign as equivalence
examples: The study used the TNRF to inform a deductive coding scheme with subcodes under each noticing dimension, applied to reflection papers and chat interactions
key_sources: Selen Galiç, Mathias Tejera, Sebastián Parodi, Markus Hohenwarter, Zsolt Lavicza. (2026). Preservice mathematics teachers' noticing in AI-based simulations: transitions among attending, interpreting, and shaping. ZDM – Mathematics Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11858-026-01805-4

article_title: Evaluation of video review tools for assessing non-technical skills in emergency department resuscitation teams: a systematic review.
citation: Alexander Emily G, Denny Fraser, Gordon Malcom WG, McKiernan Cieran, Lowe David J. (2023). Evaluation of video review tools for assessing non-technical skills in emergency department resuscitation teams: a systematic review. BMC Emergency Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12873-023-00895-7
title: Use T-NOTECHS as the tool of choice for assessing non-technical skills of ED resuscitation teams via video review
description: The review recommends T-NOTECHS for video-based assessment of NTS in ED resuscitation teams because it is validated, most studied, and balances usability, reliability and validity. It states that "when assessing NTS more holistically, T-NOTECHS demonstrates usability, reliability and validity". T-NOTECHS splits NTS into 5 categories on a 5-point Likert scale and provides score anchors to guide users.
requirements: Video recording of real-life resuscitations in the ED; reviewers can pause or rewind video for more accurate assessment
constraints: The conclusion that T-NOTECHS is the best tool is suggested but not proven fully due to small sample sizes; reliability varies across studies (ICC 0.48–0.94)
target_learning_goals: non-technical skills including leadership, communication, situational awareness, decision making and teamwork
examples: Six of the nine included studies used T-NOTECHS; the review recommends multi-centre studies with larger sample sizes to establish its utility, and suggests TTCA-24 where communication is identified as a weakness
key_sources: Alexander Emily G, Denny Fraser, Gordon Malcom WG, McKiernan Cieran, Lowe David J. (2023). Evaluation of video review tools for assessing non-technical skills in emergency department resuscitation teams: a systematic review. BMC Emergency Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12873-023-00895-7

article_title: Reliability of the assessment of non-technical skills by using video-recorded trauma resuscitations.
citation: van Maarseveen O. E. C., Ham W. H. W., Huijsmans R. L. N., Dolmans R. G. F., Leenen L. P. H. (2020). Reliability of the assessment of non-technical skills by using video-recorded trauma resuscitations. European Journal of Trauma and Emergency Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00068-020-01401-5
title: T-NOTECHS assessment tool for trauma-team non-technical skills
description: The T-NOTECHS (Trauma NOn-TECHnical Skills) is a behavioral observation instrument adapted from aviation NOTECHS to assess trauma-team non-technical skills during resuscitation. "The T-NOTECHS consists of five behavioral domains: leadership, cooperation and resource management, communication and interaction, assessment and decision making, and situation awareness/coping with stress." Each domain is scored on a five-point Likert scale (5 = perfect behavior, 1 = behavior not demonstrated), and domain scores are summed to a total from 5 to 25, where 25 indicates perfect teamwork. This study evaluated its reliability when applied to video-recorded resuscitations.
requirements: Assessors require training to align assessments; in this study training consisted of reading the Steinemann et al. article and a 2 h training session discussing T-NOTECHS assessment of resuscitations
constraints: The authors caution their results might overestimate reliability because only three trained research assistants were used, so generalization should be exercised with care
target_learners: trauma team members (trauma team leader, surgical resident, anesthetist, ED nurses, radiology technician)
target_learning_goals: non-technical team skills: leadership, cooperation, communication, decision-making, situation awareness and coping with stress
examples: Eighteen recorded videos of real trauma resuscitations were scored by three trained research assistants using a standardized Excel score sheet, blinded to each other's results
key_sources: van Maarseveen O. E. C., Ham W. H. W., Huijsmans R. L. N., Dolmans R. G. F., Leenen L. P. H. (2020). Reliability of the assessment of non-technical skills by using video-recorded trauma resuscitations. European Journal of Trauma and Emergency Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00068-020-01401-5

article_title: Becoming the Change: A Critical Evaluation of the Changing Face of Life Science, as Reflected in the NGSS
citation: Larry L Bowman, Jr. and Aimee L Govett. (2014). Becoming the Change: A Critical Evaluation of the Changing Face of Life Science, as Reflected in the NGSS. Submitted to The Science Educator. http://www.etsu.edu/cas/gk/
title: TNCSSE-NGSS Guidemaps: an 18-poster series correlating Tennessee science standards with the NGSS
description: A series of 18 posters that "serves as a series of guidemaps" linking the Tennessee Curriculum Standards for Science Education (TNCSSE) to the NGSS from kindergarten through high school. Arrows from a TNCSSE Course Level Expectation to an NGSS Disciplinary Core Idea mark correlations; missing arrows mark exclusions or entirely new inclusions. The State Board of Education steering committee asked to use the collection in its science standards review deliberations.
requirements: Both standards sets to correlate: the maps pair TNCSSE Course Level Expectations with NGSS Disciplinary Core Ideas and their printed explanations
constraints: Unequal weighting: "every arrow is not equally weig hted," as a TNCSSE CLE may correspond to only a small portion of a much more detailed NGSS DCI
target_learners: K-12 science educators in Tennessee adapting current and past lesson plans to NGSS standards
target_learning_goals: Aligning existing lesson plans and curriculum with NGSS standards by visualizing inclusions and exclusions between the two standards sets
examples: Presented at the November 2013 Tennessee Science Teachers Association conference and a December 2013 regional symposium; the SBE steering committee asked to use the collection in its standards review
key_sources: Larry L Bowman, Jr. and Aimee L Govett. (2014). Becoming the Change: A Critical Evaluation of the Changing Face of Life Science, as Reflected in the NGSS. Submitted to The Science Educator. http://www.etsu.edu/cas/gk/

article_title: Changes to the TN Middle Grades Science Curriculum According to NGSS
citation: Bowman, Jr., Larry L. and Govett, Aimee Lee. (2014). Changes to the TN Middle Grades Science Curriculum According to NGSS. As submitted to Tennessee Educational Leadership Journal on March 28, 2014. http://www.etsu.edu/cas/gk/
title: Eighteen correlation posters (guidemaps) mapping Tennessee Science Standards to NGSS across kindergarten through high school
description: A set of 18 posters created by STEM Fellow Larry Bowman showing the correspondence between the current Tennessee Science Education standards (Huffman, 2009) and the NGSS (Achieve, 2013). The article describes them as "a series of guidemaps betwee n the Tennessee Curriculum Standards for Science Education (TNCSSE) for grade levels kindergarten through high school and the corresponding NGSS." They were built as tools for educators doing curriculum development and revision and are accessible on the GK-12 Program Website.
requirements: Accessed via the GK-12 Program Website for educators conducting curriculum development and revision
target_learners: K-12 science students in Tennessee whose curricula the posters map
target_learning_goals: Alignment of state science curriculum standards with the Next Generation Science Standards across all grade bands
examples: The posters specifically address the NGSS Middle Grades Disciplinary Core Ideas as compared to the existing 6-8 Tennessee Science Standards
key_sources: Bowman, Jr., Larry L. and Govett, Aimee Lee. (2014). Changes to the TN Middle Grades Science Curriculum According to NGSS. As submitted to Tennessee Educational Leadership Journal on March 28, 2014. http://www.etsu.edu/cas/gk/

article_title: Online Support System for Transnational Education
citation: Spichkova M, Harland J, Alharthi A. (2016). Online Support System for Transnational Education. International Conference on Engineering Education and Research 2016, Sydney, Australia. https://www.rmit.edu.au
title: TNE Online Support System with an online module and quiz plus an automated assistance module
description: The proposed TNE online support system consists of two core parts: an online module on TNE-related topics with a corresponding quiz, and an automated assistance module. The module is designed to "ensure that students understand TNE-related potential problems, such as the importance of submission deadlines", while the assistance module provides advice on studying and living in Australia, tailored to a specific institution. The system is intended for onshore international students and offshore TNE students, including RMIT's Vietnam campuses.
requirements: The TNE Online Module should be completed by both staff and students at the beginning of their study, as a final stage of the enrollment process
constraints: The system is intended as a replacement for many of the typical queries asked by students, but not as a complete replacement for human advisors
target_learners: internationally mobile students and onshore international students in transnational higher education
target_learning_goals: understanding TNE-related potential problems such as submission deadlines and plagiarism issues
accessing advice on studying and living in the host country
examples: RMIT already uses online modules for induction and training of new staff members on topics such as Health and Safety
key_sources: Spichkova M, Harland J, Alharthi A. (2016). Online Support System for Transnational Education. International Conference on Engineering Education and Research 2016, Sydney, Australia. https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.05111
